boundary: Pass 5984 shows the other lane's determinant map is the n=2 case of a standard construction. That is a LOCATION result, not a refutation: their M_2(F_2) identification remains exactly true. Pass 5987 records that det is not the unique invariant with the property

pass_5984_the_ladder_is_immediate.conclusion: the whole BT1707 contextuality ladder -- W(1,2), W(3,2), W(5,2) -- comes from one quadratic form. Their determinant is the n=2 shadow of it, and no 3x3 matrix algebra is needed for the three-qubit rung
pass_5984_the_ladder_is_immediate.the_observation: that is not really about matrices. It is the quadratic form Q(x,z) = sum_i x_i z_i on F_2^(2n), and M_2(F_2) is 4-dimensional only because 2n = 4 when n = 2
pass_5984_the_ladder_is_immediate.what_this_does_to_their_result: nothing negative. M_2(F_2) with det polarization IS the two-qubit symplectic form, exactly as they proved. What changes is that it is an INSTANCE of a construction that runs up the whole ladder, so the natural generalisation is in n, not in q

pass_5986_the_two_directions.in_n: Q(x,z) = sum x_i z_i on F_2^(2n) gives W(2n-1,2) for every n (this pass)
pass_5986_the_two_directions.in_q: det on M_2(F_q) gives W(3,q) for even q and a quadric for odd q (Passes 5936, 5976)
pass_5986_the_two_directions.so: the construction generalises cleanly in BOTH directions, and they are independent: q controls whether the ambient is symplectic or orthogonal, n controls the rank

pass_5987_det_is_not_unique.answer: NO. Any nondegenerate quadratic form on F_q^4 has an alternating polarization in characteristic 2, so det is one of many
pass_5987_det_is_not_unique.question: is det the only degree-2 invariant that works at even q?
pass_5987_det_is_not_unique.what_singles_it_out: that it is the natural ALGEBRA invariant of M_2, not that it has a property no other form has

pass_5988_the_63.answer: NO -- 63 = 2^6 - 1 is the point count of PG(5,2) and nothing else here
